quest.title: The Shadows Deepen
quest.description: Having been invited to serve as instructors at the Adventurers' Guild winter camp, you reach an agreement with Albedo, who is also conducting research in the mountains, to find out what happened here. The path towards the truth is winding and long, and you keep encountering new things...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000, Unknown Item #373335 x1

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Hey! Good morning!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: I slept great last night! How about you guys? All rested up?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I'm fine, as usual.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I slept pretty well, too.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The path down the mountain is easier to follow in the daylight. Let's take this chance to head down to the base camp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go! If we make good time, maybe we can all get lunch together.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon! Are you alright? Are you hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Paimon's fine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm okay. You?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Phew... That's good... My arm got a little scratched up, but it's nothing serious.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Eula, how about you?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I'm okay. But I don't see the other two. I'm afraid... the avalanche may have pushed them off the cliff.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They fell down!? Th—They'll be okay, though, right...?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I think they're both robust enough to survive the fall. But if the falling debris knocked them unconscious, and they're lying there in the freezing cold...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: We have to get down there and rescue them, immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Okay, let's move!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hang in there, guys...

talks.objective: Head beneath the cliff to look for your companions

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bennett!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Bennett, are you okay!? Shout if you can hear me! Bennett!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: A voice — over there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bennett, is that you!?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Guys... I'm over here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright? Are you hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I—I... lemme check...

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'm a little dizzy, but I'm not in any pain... I don't think I'm injured.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Thank goodness... scared the life out of me.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: If you're dizzy, sit and rest for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Ah, it's fine, really. This kind of thing happens all the time, I'll be fine. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Oh, wait, where's Albedo? Isn't he with you guys?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We thought he fell off the cliff with you... He still hasn't shown up...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: We've found Bennett here, so Albedo can't be far away. Keep searching this area.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Got it!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Traveler, I know what that look means. What's on your mind?

choices.text: ...I have a bad feeling about this.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Maybe seasoned veterans have an instinct for it.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: I sense it too. Something seems to have changed, but I can't confirm for sure... it could be difficult to verify.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What could it be...)

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: It might be... imprudent to speculate out loud. But I believe you know what I am referring to.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Traveler, I think...

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: You...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Watch out!

choices.text: It's like something bad's about to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Well? Any sign of him?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Not a trace.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Nothing from me, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange, we didn't have any luck, either... Where could he have gone...?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: ...Everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Albedo!? Are... are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Nothing serious.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Okay. Everyone accounted for.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Guys, I—I think... it's gotta be because of me. The avalanche only happened because I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I guess flipping a Treasure Hoarder Insignia isn't gonna change my luck after all... No wonder no one wants to go adventuring with me. *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Don't say that. I'm hardly the lucky type myself, so I'm not about to go blaming every little thing that goes wrong on you.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Exactly! Besides, Dragonspine is a dangerous place. Avalanches literally come with the territory. Bad luck has nothing to do with it, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Was that really an accident?)

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Traveler, what's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your face looks... *gasp* Oh no! Did you get hit on the head!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Everyone, the incident is behind us now. We should keep moving.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Why do I feel that Dragonspine has become more dangerous than it used to be... I hope it's just my imagination...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Our top priority now is to get off the mountain and regroup with the adventurers. Whatever further dangers this mountain has to throw at us, we must face them together.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Agreed. Guys, keep your eyes peeled and watch your step. Careful does it.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Whew! We've been heading in the right direction for a good length of time now — we must be getting close, I can feel it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Victory is in sight, hooray!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As soon as we get to base camp, Paimon wants a bowl of hot soup and some barbecued meat!

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I hope we can all get there safely. No more incidents, please...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Weird things have been happening this whole trip... Something feels wrong, but what is it...?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, what's on your mind? You seem a little distracted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something's up, isn't it? Uhh... are you hungry? Cold? Shall Paimon hug your head to warm you up?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks, but I'm alright, Paimon.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: I don't think I've spent so much time on Dragonspine before. It sure is cold, but the view is amazing! Isn't it, Eula?

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: Eula?

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Sorry, I wasn't listening. What did you say?

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: I was just thinking — whenever I've met up with you at Dragonspine in the past, we always stick to the same few spots. It's much more vast and beautiful here than I realized.

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: If it were a little warmer and a little safer, I bet this place would be bustling with visitors.

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: I agree... People are put off by the cold and have an aversion to danger. They don't realize that there is much to explore beneath the icy exterior, if you are willing to spend the time and energy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Something seemed to grab Eula's attention. Does she sense that something's off, too?)

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: Albedo, is this the way down?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I think there are several routes in this area, hmm, does the path fork off here? It looks like it does... hmm, but maybe it doesn't... my head's still a little fuzzy from the impact...

response.speaker: Amber
response.text: I'm kind of dizzy, too. I keep thinking things are swaying a little... Maybe I'm just hungry?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Either path will work for us. The smaller trail is less worn and harder to see, but it's also shorter. Since everyone is weary, I suggest we take the shortcut.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Follow me.

choices.text: With some things, I don't know where to begin.

talks.objective: Go to the place Albedo mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Wait.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Bennett and Amber don't look well. Can we take a break? We can continue once their conditions have improved.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Ugh... Now that you mention it...

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Huh? I...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: You hit your head earlier, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Oh, y—you noticed. Hehe... Are you sure it's worth holding everyone up over a little thing like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem at all, health and safety always come first!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Take a break, both of you.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Okay... Sorry for this. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Yeah... thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Drinking some water can help with the dizziness! Oh, and uh, lying flat on your back helps too.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Thank you, Bennett. Seems like you really know your stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Haha... Well, when life gives you lemons...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Bennett, weren't you feeling dizzy too? Stop pushing yourselves, both of you. Get some rest, we'll continue when you've gathered your energy.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Pfft...

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Eula might come off as a little frosty, but she takes caring for her friends super seriously, more than anyone else I know. Every time I see that look on her face, I'm just like... Aah! Stop staring at me!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What in the world was that thing!? One moment it was human, the next it was a plant...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Is everyone alright?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: We're fine. But can you please tell us what's going on? I—I don't understand...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I take it this monster is whom I had the pleasure of meeting last time.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As you might have guessed, this is a mutated whopperflower. An extremely rare kind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But can whopperflowers turn into humans?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Not typically. But conditions on Dragonspine are far from typical.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Perhaps the dragon's blood seeped into the land, then was passed to the monsters via the ley lines, accelerating their rate of mutation.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: How could that happen!?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This mountain is home to the remains of Durin, the venomous dragon. If there is anywhere in the world one might expect life to do unfathomable things, it would most likely be here.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Durin was an artificially created life form. Its existence is nothing short of a miracle, and proof of countless possibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In other words, this mountain we stand on is a cradle of life's profoundest mysteries... A vast and terrifying hotbed of possibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: The avalanche... it must have been the work of this impostor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think so, too.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Agreed. All the other troubles you faced on the way down could also have been its handiwork. My guess is that it was targeting everyone that I've had contact with.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did this whopperflower steal your alchemy notes, too?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Right! I forgot all about that!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's not inconceivable.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: But... what was its purpose? Was it just trying to get rid of us?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I have a preliminary hypothesis on this.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Whopperflowers are masters of mimicry, and those we encounter in the wild often appear in the vicinity of the plants they impersonate.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In other words, the whopperflower likely has an instinct to "replicate and replace."

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As a plant, it will disguise itself as another plant and infiltrate the group, hiding among them for cover. The plant being imitated has no way to detect or fight back against this behavior.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But when it disguises itself as a human...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It wanted to replace you and infiltrate our group?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes. Maybe it created the avalanche to get rid of us. I predicted this eventuality, so I availed myself of the avalanche to hide and lure it out.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It was watching us the whole time, and when it saw that I had disappeared, its instinct was to take my place. At that point, its disguise was complete and its next move was to hunt its prey.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Yes, that's exactly how whopperflowers operate.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: So when it approached and attacked Joel... what was that? A trial run?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Perhaps... Or maybe it enjoyed posing as a human and wanted to experience what it felt like to be human.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: We're fortunate to have discovered it in time. I think the Traveler was the first person other than Albedo to notice something was wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Eula, you were very perceptive too.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Traveler, how could you tell the real me and my impostor apart?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I wanna know, too! I had no idea the other guy was an impostor... They looked exactly the same to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The impostor didn't have a star-shaped mark on its neck.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It goes to show how difficult it is to impersonate a human. This mutant whopperflower tried its best to replicate the original exactly, but still managed to miss some details.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Unbelievable... to think that Dragonspine creates such terrifying possibilities...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A whopperflower... it adds up, but a piece of the puzzle is still missing...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Was this the same one we met on the day we were chasing the thief? It didn't feel quite the same... Could the whopperflower's mutation be unstable?)

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Anyway, at least we won in the end. It looks like my method did work after all — I used up all the bad luck, and the good luck finally came through!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: About that...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If you're referring to having fallen down the mountain and avoided injury, well, that's because I was secretly protecting you.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Huh? Uhh... well that still counts as good luck to me!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Haha, yes, that's not an unreasonable way of looking at it.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Okay. We've been delayed long enough. Time to move on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Woohoo! I'm back!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Cyrus doesn't seem to be here... He must have headed up the mountain. Let's wait for him here.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Amber, are you feeling better?

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Yep! All good now. Nothing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I don't know what I'd do without you guys... if not for you, I'd probably still be locked up in that cage...

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I really wanna thank you all properly, but I can't think how at the moment...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You must be pretty used to being on the receiving end of people's kindness by now, though, surely? You probably need it often enough given your... situation, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...Come on, don't put it like that.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Sure, plenty of people have shown me kindness before. But that doesn't mean I will ever take it for granted. No matter how many times people help me out in life, I will never forget any of them.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, instead of repaying those who helped you, perhaps you could help others yourself? Everyone meets others in need from time to time. By choosing to be there for them, you're passing the kindness you received onto others.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Yep, you're right. That's what I've always tried to do and will always continue to do.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could start with helping rookie adventurers.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Hahaha, right! And when Cyrus gets back, I'll find some way to help him out, too!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Phew... This has been quite an eventful day.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Yeah, it has! It's really hit me how tired I am now that I've started to relax...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: I need to rest. Everyone, please excuse me for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Yeah, I need to get some water and maybe a piece of fruit. Once I'm rested up, I need to get back to being an instructor again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, well it looks like the curse of the mountaineers who couldn't get off the mountain is finally broken.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Feels like an action-packed chapter has come to a close. Shall we find somewhere to rest and chat, too?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Why not. Then, please come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Knew he had something to say to me...)

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You sensed something too, didn't you? Then let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you going back to your camp again? Paimon thought maybe we could talk here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Come on, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, okay... might as well come with you...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Good. Shall we set off right away?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Sorry for bringing you back here once again. Some topics are best discussed in private.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this about the impostor?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I have to say, Traveler... I'm very surprised you noticed the difference between me and the impostor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you mean the mark on your neck...?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes. This mark... perhaps it's where it all began.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Sounds like the beginning of a big story, keep going!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, I can't deny that what I'm about to say does sound like something from a children's storybook.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So, what do you think this diamond-shaped mark means?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... A tattoo? A crest? ...Something else?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A scar?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: No. Consider it... a birthmark.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Have you ever seen an intricate glass ornament and wondered how it was made? Well, one method for crafting with glass is a technique known as "glassblowing."

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Glassblowing is not a widely known art in Teyvat. For this reason, glassware made in this way is usually very expensive.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As the name implies, glassblowing involves blowing air into a hole, much like blowing up a balloon.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This type of glassware is known for having a "pontil mark" at the point where the blowpipe was inserted, where the hole was sealed at the very end. This mark is a sign that the item was crafted by a human hand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds kind of amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It is a wondrous and beautiful art form. Alice says that these marks are seen as proof of the maker's fine handiwork, the only flaw in an otherwise perfect work of art.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: My mark is something similar to this.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The difference between synthetic and natural life lies in the directional flow of the life force.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The energy of a natural life form flows out from within. That's why flower buds bloom and curled leaves unfold. It is the very reason we watch in wonder at blossoming flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Creating life artificially, on the other hand, involves — to a certain extent — the introduction of an external source of energy into the embryonic life form. When the hole where the life force was infused is sealed at the end, it leaves a mark not dissimilar to the pontil mark in blown glass wares.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The alchemical substance drips and spreads out in all directions, resulting in this rather ingenious diamond shape.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so that's where it came from...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This mark is a sign of my artificial origins, and proof of my imperfection as a human.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I presume that the impostor intentionally avoided replicating this mark, so as not to become less than perfect himself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Should you be telling me all this?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You are fundamentally different from other people. I have few qualms about sharing my secrets with you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Just as Paimon said, it all sounds like a story. Even if you were to tell anyone else, they would regard it as nothing more than a tall tale.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The transcendent and miraculous are not the only things to which human beings aspire. They pursue the everyday, the ordinary, to a far greater extent than I would have ever imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hence the notion of "otherness."

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: People like to believe that those who are thoroughly different from themselves could only ever exist in stories. It makes things much easier.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Or in other words, all the unfathomable things we have seen recently would make good material for a novel.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I have friends who write novels. If they wrote this story, it would probably be even more complex.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Making up stories is easy. Even Paimon can do that!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh? I didn't know you had that kind of talent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, Paimon's the best guide in Teyvat. Making up stories is a piece of cake.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: In that case, how about we have a storytelling contest?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We can base our stories on the events of the last few days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds great! But we still have to help out the Adventurers' Guild...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I understand. Creativity is something that cannot be rushed. Take your time, and come back when you have found some inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We'll see whose story is more compelling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Deal!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we'll regroup with the Adventurers' Guild for now!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: You examine the picture...
dialogues.text: (This artwork is, to the last stroke, one made with extreme aesthetic sense. Paimon looks elegant and dignified, and she wears an enigmatic but romantic smile, her upturned lips displaying a vast brilliance beyond human ken. Very pretty, of course, but this isn't the Paimon you know at all...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... no response. Are we definitely looking in the right place?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's not here either. Hmm... Let's check in with the others.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Brace yourselves. This will be a challenge.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Stay back. I'm going to cut this weed down to size!
